s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, painful, and tender skin and mucous membrane lesions with ulcerations, associated with systemic inflammation and lymph node involvement
salient_findings: Recurrent ankle swelling and painful nodules on legs and feet
Painful leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders
Intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations
Systemic inflammation with elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Lymph node involvement with splenomegaly
key_facts: 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and painful nodules
Symptoms worsened during two pregnancies
Nodules progressed to painful leg ulcers
Developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations
Previous treatments included wound care, systemic corticosteroids, and immunosuppressants
Large, tender, irregularly shaped leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders
Reticulated erythema and purpura present on hands
Genital and oral ulcers present
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Mildly elevated C3 and leukocytosis
Hyperglycemia present
Doppler ultrasound showed venous stasis
Systemic imaging revealed splenomegaly and lymph node involvement
Skin biopsy showed monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Behcet's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent oral and genital ulcers, skin lesions, and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy and abnormal T-cell population on flow cytometry

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Painful leg ulcers with violaceous and purpuric borders

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of tender skin lesions, fever, and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent skin lesions, oral and genital ulcers, and systemic inflammation with elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

raw.rationale: The presence of monomorphic, perivascular, and periadnexal atypical lymphocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy, along with immunohistochemical staining showing CD3-positive T cells and flow cytometry revealing a phenotypically abnormal T-cell population, strongly supports the diagnosis of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Behcet's disease
rejected.why: While oral and genital ulcers are present, the key distinguishing feature of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is the atypical lymphocytic infiltrate, which is not characteristic of Behcet's disease.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: The presence of atypical lymphocytic infiltrate and abnormal T-cell population on flow cytometry is not consistent with Pyoderma gangrenosum, which typically presents with neutrophilic infiltrate.

rejected.label: Sweet syndrome
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic histopathological features of Sweet syndrome, such as dense neutrophilic infiltrate, and the presence of atypical lymphocytic infiltrate, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While some features, such as reticulated erythema and purpura, may be seen in Systemic lupus erythematosus, the presence of atypical lymphocytic infiltrate and abnormal T-cell population is more characteristic of Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
